kinds.name: OpenID Connect
kinds.description: Sign in through any OpenID Connect provider: Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Keycloak, Authentik and others.

fields.label: Issuer URL
fields.help: The provider's issuer. Pando reads <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration for the rest.

fields.label: Client ID
fields.help: The client ID of the web application you registered for Pando.

fields.label: Client secret
fields.help: The application's client secret. Stored encrypted and never shown again.

fields.label: Scopes
fields.help: Space-separated. Add groups if your provider needs a scope to send them.

fields.label: Groups claim
fields.help: The claim that lists the person's groups. Each one becomes a synced group in Pando.

fields.label: Subject claim
fields.help: The claim that identifies a person and never changes. Microsoft Entra ID needs oid.

fields.label: Username claim
fields.help: The claim holding the person's username in Pando.

fields.label: Email claim
fields.help: The claim holding the person's email address.

fields.label: Name claim
fields.help: The claim holding the person's display name. When it is empty, given_name and family_name are used.

fields.label: Google Workspace domain
fields.help: Only accept Google accounts from this domain. Without it, anyone with a Google account can sign in.

fields.label: Prompt
fields.help: Ask the provider to always show its sign-in form or account chooser.

fields.label: Skip the userinfo endpoint
fields.help: Use only the ID token's claims. By default Pando fills in missing claims from userinfo.

fields.label: Session length
fields.help: How long a sign-in lasts. Without SCIM this is also how long access can outlive its removal at the provider.

presets.label: Microsoft Entra ID
presets.help: Groups arrive as object IDs, and Entra does not vouch for email addresses, so accounts are never linked by email.

presets.label: Google Workspace
presets.help: Google sends no groups, so access is given through Pando's own groups.

presets.label: Authentik
presets.help: Authentik sends group names in the profile scope.

do.text: In the Admin Console, open **Applications and Resources** → **Applications**.
Choose **Create App Integration**, then **Classic experience**.
Choose **OIDC - OpenID Connect**, then **Web Application**, then **Next**.
Set **Sign-in redirect URIs** to `{callback_url}`.
Under **Assignments**, choose who can sign in, then choose **Save**.
On the **General** tab, copy the **Client ID** and the client secret.

To sign in from the Okta dashboard, choose **Edit** under **General Settings**, set **Login initiated by** to **Either Okta or App**, **Login flow** to **Redirect to app to initiate login (OIDC Compliant)** and **Initiate login URI** to `{login_url}`, then choose **Save**.
On the app's **Sign On** tab, choose **Edit** under **OpenID Connect ID Token**.
Set **Group claims filter** to `groups`, **Matches regex** and `.*`, then choose **Save**.
In the Microsoft Entra admin center, open **Entra ID** → **App registrations** and choose **New registration**.
Under **Supported account types**, choose **Single tenant only**, then choose **Register**.
Copy the **Application (client) ID** and **Directory (tenant) ID** from **Overview**.
Under **Manage**, open **Authentication** and choose **Add Redirect URI**.
Choose **Web**, set **Redirect URI** to `{callback_url}`, and choose **Configure**.
To sign in from My Apps, open **Branding & properties** and set **Home page URL** to `{login_url}`.
Open **Certificates & secrets** → **Client secrets** and choose **New client secret**.
Choose an expiry, then choose **Add**.
Copy its **Value**, not its **Secret ID**.
Under **Manage**, open **Token configuration** and choose **Add groups claim**.
Choose **Groups assigned to the application**, then choose **Add**.
In **Entra ID** → **Enterprise apps**, open the app and set **Assignment required?** to **Yes** under **Properties**.
Under **Users and groups**, choose **Add user/group** and add the groups that use Pando.
Under **API permissions**, keep **Microsoft Graph** → **User.Read**.
In Google Cloud, open **Google Auth Platform** → **Clients** and choose **Create client**.
Set **Application type** to **Web application**.
Under **Authorized redirect URIs**, add `{callback_url}`, then choose **Create**.
Copy the **Client ID** and **Client secret**. Google shows the secret once.
On **Audience**, set **User type** to **Internal**.
In the Admin Console, choose your realm, then **Clients** → **Create client**.
Set **Client type** to **OpenID Connect**, enter a **Client ID**, and choose **Next**.
Turn on **Client authentication**, keep **Standard flow** on, and choose **Next**.
Set **Valid redirect URIs** to `{callback_url}` and **Home URL** to `{login_url}`, then choose **Save**.
On the **Credentials** tab, copy the **Client Secret**.
On the client's **Client scopes** tab, open the scope ending `-dedicated`.
Choose **Configure a new mapper**, or **Add mapper** → **By configuration**, then **Group Membership**.
Set **Name** and **Token Claim Name** to `groups`, turn off **Full group path**, and choose **Save**.
In the Admin interface, open **Applications** → **Applications** and choose **New Application**.
Name the application and note its **Slug**.
Under **UI Settings**, set **Launch URL** to `{login_url}`, then choose **Next**.
Choose **OAuth2/OpenID Connect**, then choose **Next**.
Set **Client type** to **Confidential**.
Add a **Strict** redirect URI of `{callback_url}`.
Choose a **Signing Key**.
Copy the **Client ID** and **Client Secret**, then choose **Submit**.

steps.label: Application
steps.title: Register Pando as a web application

do.text: In your provider, create an OpenID Connect web application that uses the authorization code flow.
Set its redirect URI to `{callback_url}`.
To sign in from the provider's dashboard, set its initiate login URI to `{login_url}`.
Copy its issuer, client ID and client secret.
Add a claim listing the person's groups to the ID token or userinfo.

kinds.name: SAML 2.0
kinds.description: Sign in through a SAML 2.0 identity provider. Pando publishes its own metadata for the provider to import.

fields.label: Provider metadata URL
fields.help: Where the provider publishes this application's metadata. Pando re-reads it daily, so certificate rollovers are followed.

fields.label: Provider metadata XML
fields.help: Or paste the metadata instead of giving a URL.

fields.label: NameID format
fields.help: What Pando asks the provider to identify people by. The NameID must never change for a person.

options.label: Unspecified
options.description: Whatever the provider is set to send.

options.label: Persistent
options.description: An opaque ID that never changes.

fields.label: Groups attribute
fields.help: The attribute listing the person's groups. Empty tries groups, memberOf, member and Microsoft's groups claim.

fields.label: Subject attribute
fields.help: Identify people by this attribute instead of the NameID.

fields.label: Email attribute
fields.help: Empty tries email, mail and Microsoft's emailaddress claim.

fields.label: Name attribute
fields.help: Empty tries displayName, name, and first and last name.

fields.label: Username attribute
fields.help: The attribute holding the person's username in Pando. Empty tries username, uid, login and Microsoft's name claim.

fields.label: The provider's email addresses are verified
fields.help: Only if people cannot set their own email in the provider. Needed to link accounts by email.

fields.label: Allow sign-in from the provider's dashboard
fields.help: Off is safer: a sign-in the provider starts is not tied to the browser that presents it.

fields.label: Session length
fields.help: How long a sign-in lasts. Without SCIM this is also how long access can outlive its removal at the provider.

presets.label: Okta
presets.help: The Metadata URL is on the app's Sign On tab.

presets.label: Microsoft Entra ID
presets.help: The App Federation Metadata Url is under SAML Certificates on the app's Single sign-on page.

presets.label: Google Workspace
presets.help: Google offers the IdP metadata as a download when you add the app, not as a URL.

presets.label: Keycloak
presets.help: The metadata is at /realms/<realm>/protocol/saml/descriptor on your Keycloak host.

presets.label: Authentik
presets.help: Copy download URL, under Related objects on the provider's page, gives the metadata URL.

steps.label: App
steps.title: Create a SAML app in Okta

do.text: In the Admin Console, open **Applications** → **Applications** and choose **Create App Integration**.
Choose **SAML 2.0**, then **Next**, and name the app.
Set **Single sign-on URL** to `{callback_url}`.
Set **Audience URI (SP Entity ID)** to `{entity_id}`.
Set **Name ID format** to **Persistent**.
Under **Attribute Statements**, add these:
Under **Group Attribute Statements**, add `groups` with the filter **Matches regex** `.*`.
Choose **Next**, then **Finish**.
On the **Assignments** tab, assign the people or groups who may sign in.
On the **Sign On** tab, copy the **Metadata URL**.
In the Microsoft Entra admin center, open **Entra ID** → **Enterprise apps** → **All applications**.
Choose **New application**, then **Create your own application**.
Name it, choose **Integrate any other application you don't find in the gallery (Non-gallery)**, and choose **Create**.
Open **Single sign-on** and choose **SAML**.
In **Basic SAML Configuration**, choose **Edit**.
Set **Identifier (Entity ID)** to `{entity_id}`.
Set **Reply URL (Assertion Consumer Service URL)** to `{callback_url}`, then choose **Save**.
In **Attributes & Claims**, choose **Edit**, then **Add a group claim**.
Choose **Groups assigned to the application**.
Set **Source attribute** to **Cloud-only group display names**, then choose **Save**.
Under **Users and groups**, choose **Add user/group** and assign the people or groups who may sign in.
On **Single sign-on**, under **SAML Certificates**, copy the **App Federation Metadata Url**.
In the Admin console, open **Menu** → **Apps** → **Web and mobile apps**.
Choose **Add App**, then **Add custom SAML app**, name it, and choose **Continue**.
Download the **IDP metadata** and choose **Continue**.
Open the downloaded file and paste its contents here.
Set **ACS URL** to `{callback_url}`.
Set **Entity ID** to `{entity_id}`.
Set **Name ID format** to **EMAIL** and **Name ID** to **Basic Information > Primary email**, then choose **Continue**.
Choose **Add mapping** for each of these:
Under **Group membership (optional)**, choose the groups to send and set **App attribute** to `groups`.
Choose **Finish**.
Open **User access**, choose **On for everyone**, and choose **Save**.
In the realm's admin console, open **Clients** and choose **Create client**.
Set **Client type** to **SAML** and **Client ID** to `{entity_id}`, then choose **Next**.
Set **Valid redirect URIs** to `{callback_url}`, then choose **Save**.
On the **Settings** tab, set **Name ID format** to **persistent** and choose **Save**.
On the **Keys** tab, turn off **Client signature required**.
On the **Client scopes** tab, open the client's **-dedicated** scope.
Choose **Add predefined mapper** and add **X500 email**, **X500 givenName** and **X500 surname**.
Choose **Add mapper** → **By configuration** → **User Property**, with **Property** `username` and **SAML Attribute Name** `username`.
Choose **Add mapper** → **By configuration** → **Group list**, with **Group attribute name** `groups`, and turn off **Full group path**.
Use your Keycloak host and realm in `https://<host>/realms/<realm>/protocol/saml/descriptor`.
In the Admin interface, open **Applications** → **Applications** and choose **New Application**.
Name it and choose **Next**, then choose **SAML Provider** and **Next**.
Set **ACS URL** to `{callback_url}` and **Audience** to `{entity_id}`.
Under **Advanced protocol settings**, choose a **Signing Certificate** and leave **Sign assertions** on.
Set **Service Provider Binding** to **Post**, then choose **Create Application**.
Open **Applications** → **Providers** and choose the provider.
Under **Related objects**, beside **Metadata**, choose **Copy download URL**.
Create a SAML 2.0 application.
Set its ACS URL, or reply URL, to `{callback_url}`, with the HTTP-POST binding.
Set its entity ID, or audience, to `{entity_id}`.
Or import Pando's metadata from `{entity_id}`.
Sign the response, the assertion, or both.
Assign the people or groups who may sign in.
Send each person's email, name, username and groups as attributes.

kinds.name: Cloudflare Tunnel
kinds.description: Gives apps their own hostnames through a Cloudflare Tunnel. Nothing on this machine needs to be reachable from the internet, and Cloudflare issues the certificates.

fields.label: API token
fields.help: In Cloudflare, create a custom token under Manage account, Account API tokens, or under My Profile, API Tokens. Permissions: Account / Cloudflare Tunnel / Edit; Zone / DNS / Edit; Zone / Zone / Read. Account Resources: your account. Zone Resources: the primary zone, and each secondary zone. Pando uses it to create the tunnel and to point each app's hostname at it.

fields.label: Account ID
fields.help: On your domain's Overview page in Cloudflare, under API.

fields.label: Primary zone
fields.help: A domain on your Cloudflare account. New apps are served at <app>.<zone>.

fields.label: Secondary zones
fields.help: More zones apps can be named in.

fields.label: Console hostname
fields.help: Where the console is served. Empty is the primary zone.

fields.label: Existing tunnel
fields.help: Leave empty and Pando creates a tunnel of its own. Or give a remotely managed tunnel's ID to use that one: Pando adds its rules and leaves the rest alone.

fields.label: cloudflared image
fields.help: Set to run a different cloudflared release than this Pando ships with.

do.text: In Cloudflare, open **Manage account** → **Account API tokens** for an account token, or **My Profile** → **API Tokens** for a user token.
Choose **Create Token**, then a custom token.
Add these permissions:
Under **Account Resources**, include your account. Under **Zone Resources**, include each zone apps will use.
Open one of your domains and copy **Account ID** from the **API** section of its **Overview** page.

kinds.name: Built in
kinds.description: Serves each app from Pando itself on its own port, with no TLS.

kinds.name: Traefik
kinds.description: Gives apps their own hostnames through a Traefik Pando runs on ports 80 and 443, with certificates.

fields.label: Base domain
fields.help: Apps are served at <app>.<base domain>. Point this domain and *.<base domain> at this machine.

fields.label: Console hostname
fields.help: Where the console is served over HTTPS.

options.label: One per hostname
options.description: Let's Encrypt checks each hostname over port 80, which has to be reachable from the internet.

options.label: One wildcard for the base domain
options.description: Covers every app before it exists. Needs your DNS provider's credentials.

options.label: None
options.description: Apps are served over plain HTTP on port 80.

fields.label: Certificate email
fields.help: The address Let's Encrypt registers the account to.

fields.label: DNS provider
fields.help: Who hosts the base domain's DNS. Another provider is entered as its code, such as gcloud or ovh.

fields.label: DNS provider credentials
fields.help: One NAME=value per line. Cloudflare: CF_DNS_API_TOKEN, or CF_API_EMAIL and CF_API_KEY. Amazon Route 53: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY and AWS_REGION (AWS_REGION can be us-east-1 for any standard AWS account, since Route 53 is global). DigitalOcean: DO_AUTH_TOKEN. Porkbun: PORKBUN_API_KEY and PORKBUN_SECRET_API_KEY. Namecheap: NAMECHEAP_API_USER and NAMECHEAP_API_KEY. For another provider, the variables Traefik's documentation lists for it.

fields.label: Pando runs Traefik
fields.help: Off for a Traefik already running on this machine.

fields.label: HTTP port
fields.help: The host port Traefik takes for HTTP.

fields.label: HTTPS port
fields.help: The host port Traefik takes for HTTPS.

fields.label: Traefik image
fields.help: Set to run a different Traefik release than this Pando ships with.

fields.label: Route delivery
fields.help: How routes reach Traefik. Use IngressRoutes with the Kubernetes runtime.

options.label: Files
options.description: Route files in a directory Traefik mounts. The Docker runtime.

options.label: IngressRoutes
options.description: IngressRoute objects Traefik watches in the cluster's API. The Kubernetes runtime.

fields.label: IngressRoute namespace
fields.help: The namespace Pando writes IngressRoute objects to, which Traefik watches.

fields.label: Kubeconfig file
fields.help: A kubeconfig file, for reaching the cluster from outside it.

fields.label: API requests a second
fields.help: The most requests a second each Pando replica makes to the cluster's API for routes.

fields.label: API request burst
fields.help: How many requests a replica may make at once above that rate. At least the requests a second.

fields.label: Configuration directory
fields.help: Where Pando writes Traefik's route files.

fields.label: Entry point
fields.help: The entry point of your Traefik that apps are served on.

fields.label: Certificate resolver
fields.help: The certificate resolver your Traefik has configured. Empty asks for no certificates.

steps.label: Your Traefik
steps.title: Point your Traefik at Pando's routes

do.text: Start Traefik with `--providers.file.directory` set to a directory, and `--providers.file.watch=true`.
Mount that directory into Pando at `/etc/traefik/dynamic`.
Copy the name of a resolver under `certificatesResolvers` in Traefik's static configuration.
At your DNS provider, add **A** records for the base domain, `*.` plus the base domain, and the console hostname, pointing at this machine's public IP address.
At the provider that hosts the base domain, create a credential with this access:

rows: API token with Zone / Zone / Read and Zone / DNS / Edit
IAM user access key allowed route53:GetChange, route53:ListHostedZonesByName, route53:ListResourceRecordSets and route53:ChangeResourceRecordSets
Personal access token with the domain:create, domain:read and domain:delete scopes
API key, with API Access turned on in the domain's details
API access, with this machine's IPv4 address whitelisted

do.text: For another provider, find its code and variables in the lego DNS provider list.
Enter each variable below as `NAME=value`, one to a line. For Route 53, add `AWS_REGION=us-east-1`.

kinds.name: BuildKit
kinds.description: Builds images from source in a rootless BuildKit that Pando runs itself.

fields.label: Build service cache
fields.help: Bytes BuildKit keeps between builds, oldest trimmed first; a negative number removes the limit.

fields.label: App build caches
fields.help: Bytes every app's build cache may use together, least recently used evicted first; a negative number removes the limit.

kinds.name: Docker
kinds.description: Runs apps as containers on a Docker host.

fields.label: Docker host
fields.help: The Docker endpoint. Empty uses the environment, which the bundled Compose file relies on.

fields.label: CPU available
fields.help: Thousandths of a core Pando may allocate.

fields.label: Memory available
fields.help: Bytes Pando may allocate.

fields.label: Disk available
fields.help: Bytes of disk Pando may allocate.

fields.label: Processes per container
fields.help: How many processes and threads each app container may run at once, so one app cannot exhaust the host's process table. A negative number removes the limit.

fields.label: App network range
fields.help: The IPv4 range each app's private network takes its addresses from. A /16 holds about 4,000 apps; a wider range such as 10.208.0.0/12 holds more. "off" uses Docker's own pool, which holds about 30 networks.

fields.label: App network size
fields.help: The size of each app's private network, as a prefix length from 24 to 29. 28 holds 13 containers; an app with more workloads than fit gets a larger network.

fields.label: Egress gateway image
fields.help: The image an app's egress gateway runs from when its egress rules restrict anything: any image with Pando's binary at /usr/local/bin/pando. Without one, and with Pando not running in a container, apps whose egress is restricted cannot be deployed.
fields.default: The image Pando's own container runs

fields.label: Container runtime
fields.help: The runtime Docker starts apps with, by the name it is registered under in daemon.json. "runsc" (gVisor) or a Kata runtime makes this a sandboxed runtime, which host policy can require; the port and file-write checks when an app is added then cannot see inside the sandbox, so Pando asks for the port instead.

kinds.name: Docker on several hosts
kinds.description: Runs apps as containers on several Docker hosts. Each app is placed on one host and stays there: a new app goes to the host with the most free memory that fits it. Pando reaches each host's apps through a forwarding agent it runs there, which accepts only Pando's certificate. Built images reach the hosts through the install's image registry.

fields.label: Hosts
fields.help: The hosts as a JSON list. Each has a name; an endpoint (unix:///var/run/docker.sock, tcp://host:2376 with the Docker TLS credential, or ssh://user@host with the SSH key and the host's ssh_host_key); an agent_address where Pando reaches the host's agent; and optionally no_placement to keep new apps off it. Exactly one is "control": true, the host Pando runs on.

fields.label: Agent certificate authority
fields.help: The output of `pando host-agent new-authority`. Pando issues its own certificate and each agent's from it.

fields.label: Docker TLS client certificate
fields.help: For tcp:// hosts: the CA (ca.pem), the client certificate (cert.pem) and its key (key.pem), pasted together.

fields.label: SSH private key
fields.help: For ssh:// hosts: an unencrypted private key for a user in the docker group, or root.

fields.label: Agent image
fields.help: The image of Pando each host's agent and each restricted app's egress gateway run. Every host must be able to pull it.
fields.default: The image Pando's own container runs

fields.label: Agent port
fields.help: The one port each host publishes, for its agent. Restrict it to the control host's address with the host's firewall.

fields.label: App network range
fields.help: The IPv4 range each host's app networks take their addresses from. Each host uses the whole range for its own apps. Cannot be "off" here.

fields.label: App network size
fields.help: The size of each app's private network, as a prefix length from 24 to 29.

fields.label: Container runtime
fields.help: The runtime every host's Docker starts apps with, by the name it is registered under in daemon.json, such as runsc.

do.text: Install Docker Engine on each host. Use hosts of one CPU architecture.
For a `tcp://` host, follow **Use TLS (HTTPS) to protect the Docker daemon socket** to run `dockerd --tlsverify` on port `2376`, and paste `ca.pem`, `cert.pem` and `key.pem` below.
For an `ssh://` host, use rootful Docker: over SSH, Pando reaches only `/var/run/docker.sock`, not a rootless daemon's socket.
For an `ssh://` host, run `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f pando-docker -N ""`.
On each `ssh://` host, add a user to the `docker` group with `sudo usermod -aG docker <user>` and add `pando-docker.pub` to its `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`.
Paste `pando-docker` below.
On each host, allow port `7443` from the control host's address only.
On each host, let Docker pull from the install's image registry: trust its certificate, or list it under `insecure-registries` in `/etc/docker/daemon.json`.
Give each host a `name` and an `endpoint`: `tcp://<host>:2376` or `ssh://<user>@<host>`.
Mark the host Pando runs on with `"control": true` and give it an `agent_address`, such as `10.0.0.5:7443`.
For each `ssh://` host, set `ssh_host_key` to its line from `ssh-keyscan -t ed25519 <host>`.
On the host Pando runs on, run `pando host-agent new-authority`, or `docker compose exec pando pando host-agent new-authority` with Docker Compose.
Paste its output below.

kinds.name: Incus virtual machines
kinds.description: Runs each app in its own Incus virtual machine, so no two apps share a kernel. Incus decides which cluster member a VM runs on. Pando reaches each VM through a forwarding agent it runs there, and a network ACL admits nothing else. Built images reach the VMs through the install's image registry. The edge keeps running on the Docker runtime.

fields.label: Incus address
fields.help: unix:///var/lib/incus/unix.socket when Pando runs on the Incus server, or https://host:8443 with a client certificate.

fields.label: Server certificate
fields.help: For an https:// address: /var/lib/incus/server.crt on the Incus server, or cluster.crt on a cluster.

fields.label: TLS client certificate
fields.help: For an https:// address: a client certificate and its key, as PEM, added with `incus config trust add-certificate`.

fields.label: Network
fields.help: The Incus network each app's VM is attached to. Pando must be able to reach addresses on it. On a cluster, an OVN network, or a bridge with a target member.

fields.label: Pando's addresses
fields.help: The addresses Pando connects to app VMs from, as seen on that network, as addresses or ranges.

fields.label: Agent certificate authority
fields.help: The output of `pando host-agent new-authority`. Pando issues its own certificate and each VM's agent's from it.

fields.label: Pando image
fields.help: The image of this version of Pando, which each VM's forwarding agent and each restricted app's egress gateway run. Every VM must be able to pull it.

fields.label: Project
fields.help: The Incus project VMs, volumes and the guest image are made in. A restricted client certificate must be allowed it and the network's project.

fields.label: Storage pool
fields.help: The pool for each VM's disk and the apps' volumes.
fields.default: The pool of the project's default profile's root disk

fields.label: Cluster target
fields.help: A cluster member, or @ and a cluster group, that VMs run on.
fields.default: Any member, as Incus places them

fields.label: Profiles
fields.help: Incus profiles applied to each VM. Pando sets the VM's disk and NIC itself; a profile that adds another NIC gives the VM a way in that skips Pando.

fields.label: Guest image
fields.help: An Incus image alias or fingerprint to start VMs from, with Podman serving /run/podman/podman.sock and socat installed.
fields.default: Debian 13 with Podman, prepared by Pando on first use

fields.label: Agent port
fields.help: The port each VM's agent listens on, and the only one the network ACL opens, to Pando's addresses.

fields.label: VM disk size
fields.help: Each VM's disk, in bytes, for images and what workloads write outside their volumes.

fields.label: Volume size
fields.help: The size of each app volume, in bytes, unless the app asks for more.

fields.label: VM memory overhead
fields.help: Memory each VM has beyond its app's limits, in bytes, for the guest system and Podman.

fields.label: Default CPUs
fields.help: CPUs for the VM of an app that sets no limits.

fields.label: Default memory
fields.help: Memory for the VM of an app that sets no limits, in bytes.

fields.label: App network range
fields.help: The IPv4 range app networks inside each VM take their addresses from. Must not overlap the Incus network.

fields.label: App network size
fields.help: The size of each app's private network inside its VM, as a prefix length from 24 to 29.

fields.label: CPU for Pando
fields.help: Thousandths of a core Pando may use across the members, when it shares them with other work.

fields.label: Memory for Pando
fields.help: Bytes of memory Pando may use across the members, when it shares them with other work.

steps.label: Certificates
steps.title: Connect over HTTPS
steps.lede: Skip this step for a unix:// address.

do.text: On the Incus server, run `incus config set core.https_address=:8443`.
Run `openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:3072 -nodes -days 3650 -subj /CN=pando -keyout pando.key -out pando.crt`.
Run `incus config trust add-certificate pando.crt --restricted --projects default`.
Paste `/var/lib/incus/server.crt` below, or `/var/lib/incus/cluster.crt` on a cluster.
Paste `pando.crt` and `pando.key` together below.
Run `incus network list` to see the networks.
Run `pando host-agent new-authority` and paste its output below.

kinds.name: Kubernetes
kinds.description: Runs apps as pods on the Kubernetes cluster Pando runs in, one namespace per app.

fields.label: Pod address range
fields.help: The range the cluster assigns pods. Apps may not open connections into it.

fields.label: Service address range
fields.help: The range the cluster assigns Services. Apps may not open connections into it.

fields.label: Egress gateway image
fields.help: Any image with Pando's binary at /usr/local/bin/pando. Empty, apps that restrict egress can't be deployed.

fields.label: Kubeconfig file
fields.help: A kubeconfig file, for running Pando outside the cluster during development. Pando's proxy reaches apps by cluster DNS names, so in production Pando runs inside the cluster.

fields.label: Kubeconfig context
fields.help: The context in the kubeconfig file to use.

fields.label: Pando's namespace
fields.help: Where Pando's server pods run. Apps admit connections only from Pando's server pods in this namespace.

fields.label: Pando's Service
fields.help: The Service in front of Pando's server pods, in Pando's namespace. The edge sends traffic to it.

fields.label: Pando's ServiceAccount
fields.help: The ServiceAccount Pando's server pods run as, in Pando's namespace. It is bound to the app namespace role in each app namespace.

fields.label: Proxy port
fields.help: The port Pando's proxy listens on in its pods.

fields.label: App namespace role
fields.help: The ClusterRole bound to Pando's ServiceAccount in each app namespace.

fields.label: Cluster domain
fields.help: The cluster's DNS domain, which Service names end in.

fields.label: API server address
fields.help: Only needed when the API server's address is inside the pod or Service range: the edge reads its routes from it.
fields.default: Reached by the rule for addresses outside the cluster

fields.label: Storage class
fields.help: The StorageClass app volumes are made with.

fields.label: Volume size
fields.help: Bytes for a volume whose app does not say how large it is.

fields.label: RuntimeClass
fields.help: A RuntimeClass to run apps under. One whose handler is gVisor (runsc) or Kata makes this a sandboxed runtime, which host policy can require.

fields.label: Node selector
fields.help: Run apps only on nodes with these labels, as key=value pairs separated by commas.

fields.label: Helper image
fields.help: Runs the network policy check, the port observer and volume backups. Any image with a shell, tar, wget and httpd.

fields.label: API requests a second
fields.help: The most requests a second each Pando replica makes to the cluster's API.

fields.label: API request burst
fields.help: How many requests a replica may make at once above that rate. At least the requests a second.

fields.label: Edge namespace
fields.help: The namespace the edge runs in: the Traefik that takes ports 80 and 443 and passes traffic to Pando.

fields.label: Edge replicas
fields.help: How many copies of the edge run, spread across nodes. At least 2.

options.label: LoadBalancer
options.description: The cluster's load balancer publishes ports 80 and 443.

options.label: NodePort
options.description: Every node listens on the node ports below, and a load balancer outside the cluster points at them.

fields.label: Edge HTTP node port
fields.help: The port every node listens on for the edge's HTTP.

fields.label: Edge HTTPS node port
fields.help: The port every node listens on for the edge's HTTPS.

do.text: Use a network plugin that enforces NetworkPolicy, such as Calico or Cilium.
Grant the ServiceAccount `pando` in the namespace `pando` these permissions, as `deploy/kubernetes/rbac.yaml` does:

rows: Each app namespace, through ClusterRole pando-app-manager
pods, pods/log, pods/exec, services, configmaps, secrets, persistentvolumeclaims, resourcequotas, networkpolicies
get, list, watch, create, update, patch, delete

do.text: Run `kubectl get servicecidr kubernetes` and copy **CIDRS**.
Run `kubectl cluster-info dump | grep -m1 -- --cluster-cidr` and copy the pod range. On a managed cluster, copy it from the cluster's network settings.

Choose **Create Webhook**, or **New Webhook** under **Webhooks**.
Pick the channel it posts to.
Choose **Copy Webhook URL**.

fields.label: Server
fields.help: The ntfy server.

fields.help: Seconds to wait for the server to answer.

do.text: In the ntfy app, choose **Subscribe to topic**.
Enter a **Topic name** nobody would guess.
For your own server, turn on **Use another server** and enter its address.
Choose **Subscribe**.
Sign in to the ntfy web app and open **Account**.
Under **Access tokens**, choose **Create access token**, then **Create token**.
Copy the token.

do.text: Find your email provider's SMTP server name and port.
Create SMTP credentials with your email provider, if the server requires sign-in.
Verify the address or its domain with your email provider, if it requires a verified sender.

Choose the **Send webhook alerts to a channel** template.
Check the team and channel, then select **Save**.
Copy the webhook URL from the workflow's details page.

kinds.name: Local disk

Add a lifecycle rule that deletes incomplete multipart uploads after one day.
Copy the bucket's region and, unless the store is Amazon S3, its S3 API endpoint.
Create an access key limited to the bucket, allowed these actions:
Copy the **Access key ID** and the **Secret access key**.

fields.label: Timeout

fields.help: OCI repositories to download Trivy's Java database from, comma-separated, first tried first.

fields.help: The OCI repository to download Trivy's misconfiguration checks from.

fields.label: Offline scan

kinds.name: Anthropic
kinds.description: Performs the AI functions assigned to it: repairing a failed plan, answering detection's questions, revising a plan on request, drafting access and policy, searching the audit log, and answering from the reference. Needs an Anthropic API key.

fields.label: API key
fields.help: Empty reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from Pando’s environment.

fields.label: Model
fields.help: The Claude model each function uses unless its assignment names another.

fields.label: Workspace ID
fields.help: Needed only when the API key was created for more than one workspace.

fields.label: Base URL
fields.help: A gateway or proxy in front of the Anthropic API. Empty is the API itself.

fields.label: API key variable
fields.help: The environment variable to read the key from, instead of a stored one.

do.text: In the Claude Console, open **API keys** and choose **Create key**.
Name the key and choose an expiration.
Set **Linked account** to a service account, or to yourself.
Copy the key, which starts with `sk-ant-`.

kinds.name: Local model
kinds.description: Performs the AI functions assigned to it with a model on your own hardware, through any server that speaks the OpenAI API: Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or vLLM. Nothing is sent to a provider.

fields.label: Server URL
fields.help: The server’s OpenAI-compatible address, ending in /v1. The default is Ollama on the machine running Pando’s container.

fields.label: Model
fields.help: The model each function uses unless its assignment names another, as the server names it.

fields.label: API key
fields.help: Only if your server asks for one. Stored encrypted and never shown again.

fields.label: Timeout, in seconds
fields.help: How long one request may take. Local models are slower than hosted ones.

do.text: Enter the address of the OpenAI-compatible server you run, ending `/v1`. On this machine, by its default port:
On another machine, use its address instead, such as `http://gpu.example:11434/v1`.
On Linux, a server on this machine has to listen on an address other than `127.0.0.1`, and hosted apps can reach it there too.
Enter an API key only if the server requires one: `--api-key` for `llama-server` or `vllm serve`, **Require Authentication** in LM Studio.
Enter the model's name as the server serves it:

rows: As `ollama list` shows it, after `ollama pull`
Its identifier, as `lms ls` shows it
Its `--served-model-name`, or else the model given to `vllm serve`

kinds.name: OpenAI
kinds.description: Performs the AI functions assigned to it with OpenAI's models. Uses OpenAI's Responses API, which stores each conversation on OpenAI's servers under OpenAI's retention terms; Pando does not store it. Needs an OpenAI API key.

fields.label: API key
fields.help: Empty reads OPENAI_API_KEY from Pando’s environment.

fields.label: Model
fields.help: The model each function uses unless its assignment names another.

fields.label: Base URL
fields.help: An endpoint that serves the OpenAI Responses API, such as a gateway or proxy.

fields.label: API key variable
fields.help: The environment variable to read the key from, instead of a stored one.

do.text: In the OpenAI platform, open **API keys** and choose **Create new secret key**.
Under **Permissions**, choose **Restricted** and set:
Create the key and copy it.

kinds.name: Azure DevOps
kinds.description: Clone from Azure DevOps Services or Azure DevOps Server with a personal access token, Microsoft Entra ID or an SSH key, and pick repositories from a list.

options.label: Personal access token
options.description: A token with Code (Read) scope. Works with Azure DevOps Services and Server.

options.label: Microsoft Entra ID sign-in
options.description: A person authorizes Pando with their work or school account, by device code or in the browser. Azure DevOps Services only.

options.label: Service principal
options.description: An app registration signs in with its client secret. It must be added to the organization. Azure DevOps Services only.

options.label: SSH key
options.description: A key added to a user's SSH public keys. Repositories are entered by address.

fields.label: Host
fields.help: The host repositories are on. Change it for a self-managed server.

fields.label: Organization
fields.help: The organization, or organization/project to limit the connection to one project. On Azure DevOps Server, the collection, or collection/project.

fields.label: Personal access token
fields.help: A personal access token with the Code (Read) scope.

fields.label: Directory (tenant) ID
fields.help: The app registration's directory (tenant) ID. Only a multitenant app accepts organizations.

fields.label: Application (client) ID
fields.help: The app registration's application (client) ID, from Microsoft Entra ID.

fields.label: Client secret
fields.help: Required for a service principal and for browser sign-in. Device sign-in works without one.

fields.label: SSH private key
fields.help: The private half of a deploy key or access key added to the repository. Pando reads the repository with it and never writes.

fields.label: Key passphrase
fields.help: Only if the key has one.

fields.label: Known hosts
fields.help: The host's public key, as ssh-keyscan ssh.dev.azure.com (or your server's host) prints it.

fields.label: API address
fields.help: Where the host's API is, if not where Pando would look for it.
fields.default: https://dev.azure.com/{organization}, or https://HOST/{collection} on Azure DevOps Server

fields.label: Certificate authority
fields.help: PEM certificates to trust for a self-managed host on a private certificate authority, beside the system's.

do.text: In Azure DevOps, open **User settings** → **Personal access tokens** → **New Token**.
Enter a **Name**, select the **Organization**, and set an **Expiration**. On Azure DevOps Server, select the collection.
Under **Scopes**, choose **Custom defined**, then select **Read** under **Code**.
Choose **Create** and copy the token.

steps.label: App registration
steps.title: Register an app in Microsoft Entra ID

do.text: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, open **Entra ID** → **App registrations** → **New registration**.
Enter a **Name** and choose **Register**.
For Entra ID sign-in, under **API permissions**, choose **Add a permission** → **Azure DevOps** → **Delegated permissions**, select **vso.code**, and choose **Add permissions**.
For Entra ID sign-in, under **Authentication**, set **Allow public client flows** to **Yes** and choose **Save**.
For browser sign-in, under **Authentication**, choose **Add Redirect URI** → **Web**, enter your Pando address plus `/api/v1/sources/callback`, and choose **Configure**.
For a service principal, in Azure DevOps open **Organization settings** → **Users** → **Add users**. Enter the app's name, choose **Basic** access and the projects, and choose **Add**.
On the app's **Overview**, copy the **Application (client) ID** and **Directory (tenant) ID**.
In the app registration, open **Certificates & secrets** → **Client secrets** → **New client secret**.
Enter a description, choose an expiration, and choose **Add**.
Copy the secret's **Value**.
Run `ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 3072 -f pando-azure -N ""`.
In Azure DevOps, open **User settings** → **SSH public keys** → **New Key**.
Paste `pando-azure.pub` into **Public Key Data**, enter a name, and choose **Save**.
Paste `pando-azure` below.
Run `ssh-keyscan ssh.dev.azure.com`, or your server's host, and paste its output below.

kinds.name: Bitbucket
kinds.description: Clone from Bitbucket Cloud or Bitbucket Data Center with an access token, an OAuth consumer or an SSH access key, and pick repositories from a list.

options.label: Access token
options.description: Bitbucket Cloud: a workspace, project or repository access token, or an API token. Data Center: an HTTP access token.

options.label: OAuth consumer
options.description: A person authorizes Pando in the browser. Bitbucket Cloud only.

options.label: SSH access key
options.description: A key added to a repository or project as an access key. Repositories are entered by address.

fields.label: Host
fields.help: The host repositories are on. Change it for a self-managed server.

fields.label: Workspace or project
fields.help: Bitbucket Cloud: the workspace ID, such as acme. Data Center: the project key, such as PAY. Empty is every repository the credential can read.

fields.label: Token type
fields.help: Bitbucket Cloud only. Data Center takes an HTTP access token whichever is chosen.

options.label: Access token
options.description: A workspace, project or repository access token.

options.label: API token
options.description: An Atlassian account's API token, with your Bitbucket username.

fields.label: Username
fields.help: Your username, for a Cloud API token or a Data Center personal token. Empty is x-token-auth.

fields.label: Atlassian account email
fields.help: Cloud API token only. Empty is the username.

fields.label: Token
fields.help: Read access to repositories is enough.

fields.label: OAuth consumer key
fields.help: The Key from Workspace settings → OAuth consumers.

fields.label: OAuth consumer secret
fields.help: The Secret shown beside the Key.

fields.label: SSH private key
fields.help: The private half of a deploy key or access key added to the repository. Pando reads the repository with it and never writes.

fields.label: Key passphrase
fields.help: Only if the key has one.

fields.label: Known hosts
fields.help: The host's public key, as ssh-keyscan bitbucket.org prints it. For Data Center, ssh-keyscan -p 7999 HOST, whose lines begin [HOST]:7999.

fields.label: SSH port
fields.help: Bitbucket Data Center's SSH port, for turning an HTTPS address into an SSH one. Not used on Bitbucket Cloud.

fields.label: API address
fields.help: Where the host's API is, if not where Pando would look for it.
fields.default: https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0 on Bitbucket Cloud, https://HOST/rest/api/1.0 on Data Center

fields.label: Certificate authority
fields.help: PEM certificates to trust for a self-managed host on a private certificate authority, beside the system's.

do.text: Create one of these tokens:

rows: Workspace, project or repository settings → Security → Access tokens → Create access token
Account settings → Security → Create API token with scopes → Bitbucket
Manage account, Project settings or Repository settings → HTTP access tokens → Create token

do.text: For a Cloud API token or a Data Center personal token, enter your username below.
In the workspace, open **Settings** → **Workspace settings** → **OAuth consumers** → **Add consumer**.
Enter a **Name**. Set **Callback URL** to your Pando address plus `/api/v1/sources/callback`.
Under **Permissions**, check **Repositories** **Read** and choose **Save**.
Choose the consumer's name and copy its **Key** and **Secret**.
Run `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f pando-access -N ""`.
On Bitbucket Cloud, open **Repository settings** → **Access keys** → **Add key**. Enter a **Label**, paste `pando-access.pub` into **Key** and save it.
On Data Center, open the project's or repository's **Settings** → **Access keys** → **Add key**. Paste `pando-access.pub`, choose **Read** and choose **Add key**.
Paste `pando-access` below.
Run `ssh-keyscan bitbucket.org`, or `ssh-keyscan -p 7999 HOST` for Data Center, and paste its output below.

kinds.name: Any git host
kinds.description: Clone from any git server with a username and token over HTTPS, or an SSH key. Repositories are entered by address.

options.label: Username and token
options.description: HTTPS, with an access token or password as the password.

options.label: SSH key
options.description: A deploy key. The host's public key is pinned.

fields.label: Host
fields.help: The host repositories are on. Change it for a self-managed server.

fields.label: Path prefix
fields.help: Empty is every repository on the host.

fields.label: Username
fields.help: The account the token belongs to. Empty is git.

fields.label: Token or password
fields.help: Read access to the repositories is enough.

fields.label: SSH private key
fields.help: The private half of a deploy key or access key added to the repository. Pando reads the repository with it and never writes.

fields.label: Key passphrase
fields.help: Only if the key has one.

fields.label: Known hosts
fields.help: The host's public key, as ssh-keyscan <host> prints it.

fields.label: Certificate authority
fields.help: PEM certificates to trust for a self-managed host on a private certificate authority, beside the system's.

do.text: On the git host, create an access token with read access to the repositories.
Run `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f pando-deploy -N ""`.
On the git host, add `pando-deploy.pub` to the repository as a read-only deploy key.
Paste `pando-deploy` below.
Run `ssh-keyscan` with the host's name, on a machine you trust, and paste its output below.

kinds.name: Gitea or Forgejo
kinds.description: Clone from a Gitea or Forgejo server, Codeberg included, with an access token, an OAuth2 application, or a deploy key, optionally limited to one owner.

options.label: Access token

options.description: Authorize once in the browser. Needs an address the host can send you back to.

options.label: Deploy key
options.description: An SSH key added to the repository as a deploy key. Repositories are entered by address.

fields.label: Host
fields.help: The host repositories are on. Change it for a self-managed server.

fields.label: Owner
fields.help: Limit the connection to one user's or organization's repositories, such as acme. Empty is every repository the credential can read.

fields.label: Username
fields.help: The token's account. Empty is oauth2.

fields.label: Access token
fields.help: Needs Read on repository and user.

fields.label: OAuth2 client ID
fields.help: The client ID of an OAuth2 application created under Settings → Applications, with Pando's callback as its redirect URI.

fields.label: OAuth2 client secret
fields.help: Required.

fields.label: SSH private key
fields.help: The private half of a deploy key or access key added to the repository. Pando reads the repository with it and never writes.

fields.label: Key passphrase
fields.help: Only if the key has one.

fields.label: Known hosts
fields.help: The host's public key, as ssh-keyscan <host> prints it.

fields.label: API address
fields.help: Where the host's API is, if not where Pando would look for it.

fields.label: Certificate authority
fields.help: PEM certificates to trust for a self-managed host on a private certificate authority, beside the system's.

presets.label: Codeberg
presets.help: Create an access token on Codeberg under Settings → Applications, with Read on repository and user.

do.text: Open **Settings** → **Applications**. On Forgejo, choose **New access token**.
Enter a **Token name**. Under **Repository and organization access**, choose **All (public, private, and limited)**.
Under **Select permissions**, set these:
Choose **Generate token** and copy the token.
Open **Settings** → **Applications**.
Under **Create a new OAuth2 application**, enter an **Application name**.
Set **Redirect URIs** to your Pando address plus `/api/v1/sources/callback`.
Leave **Confidential client** checked and choose **Create application**.
Copy the **Client ID** and **Client secret**.
Run `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f pando-deploy -N ""`.
In the repository, open **Settings** → **Deploy keys** → **Add deploy key** (**Add SSH key** on Gitea).
Enter a **Title**, paste `pando-deploy.pub` into **Content**, and add the key.
Paste `pando-deploy` below.
Run `ssh-keyscan` with the host's name, on a machine you trust, and paste its output below.

kinds.name: GitHub
kinds.description: Clone private repositories from github.com or GitHub Enterprise Server, and pick them from a list, with a GitHub App, an OAuth application, a personal access token or a deploy key.

options.label: GitHub App
options.description: Pando creates an App on GitHub, and you pick the repositories it reads. Tokens are short-lived.

options.label: OAuth application
options.description: Authorize as a GitHub user, with a code entered on GitHub or in the browser.

options.label: Personal access token
options.description: A fine-grained or classic token with read access to repository contents.

options.label: Deploy key
options.description: An SSH key added to one repository. Repositories are entered by address.

fields.label: Host
fields.help: The host repositories are on. Change it for a self-managed server.

fields.label: Owner
fields.help: The organization or user on GitHub. Empty is every repository the credential reaches. A GitHub App is created and installed here only; empty is your own account.

fields.label: Deploy on push
fields.help: Needs a public Pando address. Without one, Pando checks for pushes on a schedule.

fields.label: OAuth client ID
fields.help: From the OAuth application registered in GitHub under Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps, with device flow enabled.

fields.label: OAuth client secret
fields.help: Needed for browser authorization. Device authorization works without one.

fields.label: Personal access token
fields.help: A fine-grained token with read access to contents and metadata, or a classic token with the repo scope.

fields.label: SSH private key
fields.help: The private half of a deploy key or access key added to the repository. Pando reads the repository with it and never writes.

fields.label: Key passphrase
fields.help: Only if the key has one.

fields.label: Known hosts
fields.help: The host's public key, as ssh-keyscan <host> prints it. For github.com it may be left empty: Pando uses the keys GitHub publishes.

fields.label: API address
fields.help: Where the host's API is, if not where Pando would look for it.
fields.default: https://api.github.com for github.com, https://<host>/api/v3 for GitHub Enterprise Server

fields.label: Certificate authority
fields.help: PEM certificates to trust for a self-managed host on a private certificate authority, beside the system's.

presets.label: GitHub.com
presets.help: Pando creates a GitHub App for you when the connection is saved.

presets.label: GitHub Enterprise Server
presets.help: Enter the server's host. Its API is at https://<host>/api/v3 unless it was moved.

do.text: After you save, choose **Create GitHub App** on GitHub.
Pick the repositories and choose **Install**.
Back in Pando, download the logo, and upload it on the App's settings page under **Display information**.
In GitHub, open **Settings** → **Developer settings** → **OAuth apps** → **New OAuth App**.
Enter an **Application name** and **Homepage URL**. Set **Authorization callback URL** to your Pando address plus `/api/v1/sources/callback`.
Check **Enable Device Flow** and choose **Register application**.
Copy the **Client ID**. For browser sign-in, choose **Generate a new client secret**.
In GitHub, open **Settings** → **Developer settings** → **Personal access tokens** → **Fine-grained tokens** → **Generate new token**.
Set **Resource owner** to the owner. Under **Repository access**, pick the repositories.
Set **Contents** to **Read-only** and choose **Generate token**.
Run `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f pando-deploy -N ""`.
In the repository, open **Settings** → **Deploy keys** → **Add deploy key**. Paste `pando-deploy.pub` into **Key** and choose **Add key**.
Paste `pando-deploy` below.

kinds.name: GitLab
kinds.description: Clone from gitlab.com or a self-managed GitLab with an OAuth application, an access or deploy token, or a deploy key, optionally limited to one group.

options.label: OAuth application
options.description: Authorize once in the browser or with a device code. Repositories can be picked from a list.

options.label: Access token or deploy token
options.description: A personal, project or group access token, or a deploy token over HTTPS.

options.label: Deploy key
options.description: An SSH key added to the project as a deploy key. Repositories are entered by address.

fields.label: Host
fields.help: The host repositories are on. Change it for a self-managed server.

fields.label: Group
fields.help: Subgroups are included. Empty is every project the credential can read.

fields.label: OAuth client ID
fields.help: The Application ID of a GitLab OAuth application with the read_repository and read_api scopes.

fields.label: OAuth client secret
fields.help: Needed for browser authorization. Device authorization works without one.

options.label: Access token
options.description: A personal, project or group access token with read_repository and read_api. Repositories can be picked from a list.

options.label: Deploy token
options.description: A deploy token with read_repository. It cannot list repositories, so they are entered by address.

fields.label: Username
fields.help: The username GitLab shows beside the deploy token.

fields.label: Token
fields.help: An access token with read_repository and read_api, or a deploy token with read_repository.

fields.label: SSH private key
fields.help: The private half of a deploy key or access key added to the repository. Pando reads the repository with it and never writes.

fields.label: Key passphrase
fields.help: Only if the key has one.

fields.label: Known hosts
fields.help: The host's public key, as ssh-keyscan <host> prints it. Leave empty for gitlab.com; Pando knows its key.

fields.label: API address
fields.help: Where the host's API is, if not where Pando would look for it.

fields.label: Certificate authority
fields.help: PEM certificates to trust for a self-managed host on a private certificate authority, beside the system's.

do.text: In GitLab, select your avatar, then **Edit profile** → **Access** → **Applications** → **Add new application**. For a group, start from its **Settings** → **Applications**.
Enter a **Name**. Set **Redirect URI** to your Pando address plus `/api/v1/sources/callback`.
Clear **Confidential**. Under **Scopes**, select **read_repository** and **read_api**.
Choose **Save application** and copy the **Application ID** and **Secret**.
Create one of these in GitLab:

rows: Fine-grained personal access token (GitLab 19.2 or later)
Avatar → Edit profile → Access → Personal access tokens → Generate token → Fine-grained token
Code: Download, Project: Read and Branch: Read; boundary User to list every project, or the group
Avatar → Edit profile → Access → Personal access tokens → Generate token → Legacy token
Project → Settings → Access tokens → Add new token
Group → Settings → Access tokens → Add new token
Project or group → Settings → Repository → Deploy tokens → Add token

do.text: Copy the token, and for a deploy token its username.
Run `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f pando-deploy -N ""`.
In the project, open **Settings** → **Repository**, expand **Deploy keys** and choose **Add new key**.
Paste `pando-deploy.pub` into **Key** and choose **Add key**.
Paste `pando-deploy` below.

kinds.name: Amazon ECR
kinds.description: An ECR repository you created. Every build goes into it, tagged by app and deployment, and Pando gets a registry password from the access key before each push and pull.

fields.label: Registry address
fields.help: The repository's URI. It has to exist already.

fields.label: Access key ID
fields.help: An IAM user's access key that can push to, pull from and delete in the repository.

fields.label: Secret access key
fields.help: Stored encrypted, and never shown again.

fields.label: Send every build through the registry
fields.help: Even on a runtime that can take a built image directly, such as Docker on one host.

do.text: In the Amazon ECR console, choose the Region from the navigation bar.
Choose **Private repositories**, then **Create repository**.
Enter a **Repository name**, such as `pando`, and choose **Create**.
Copy the repository's **URI**.
In IAM, choose **Users**, then **Create user**.
Enter a **User name**, then choose **Next** and **Create user**.
On the user's **Permissions** tab, choose **Add permissions**, then **Create inline policy**.
Allow these actions:
On the **Security credentials** tab, choose **Create access key**, then **Other** and **Next**.
Choose **Create access key**, then **Show**.

kinds.name: OCI registry
kinds.description: A registry that signs in with a username and password, or not at all: Distribution, Harbor, GitHub Container Registry, Artifact Registry, Zot. Each app gets a repository of its own.

fields.label: Registry address
fields.help: The registry and the path to push under: ghcr.io/OWNER, a Harbor project, or an Artifact Registry repository.

fields.label: Username
fields.help: Empty for a registry Pando reaches anonymously.

fields.label: Password
fields.help: Stored encrypted, and never shown again.

options.label: A repository per app
options.description: Each app has its own, so a deleted app's images are found and removed together.

options.label: One repository for everything
options.description: For a registry where a repository has to exist before anything is pushed to it.

fields.label: Allow plain HTTP
fields.help: Only for a registry on a private network. Every host that pulls must also list it as an insecure registry.

fields.label: Send every build through the registry
fields.help: Even on a runtime that can take a built image directly, such as Docker on one host.

kinds.name: HTTPS
kinds.description: Posts every audit event, in batches as it is written, to a SIEM's HTTPS ingest endpoint: Splunk, Datadog, Elastic, Sumo Logic, Microsoft Sentinel, or anything that takes JSON with a token. A copy of the audit log leaves this installation.

fields.label: URL
fields.help: The destination's ingest endpoint. Empty when Secret URL is set.

fields.label: Secret URL
fields.help: The whole URL, for a destination whose URL carries its token, such as a Sumo Logic HTTP source.

fields.label: Token
fields.help: The API key or token the destination checks.

fields.label: Body
fields.help: The shape of each POST's body.

options.label: NDJSON
options.description: One event per line.

options.label: JSON array
options.description: The batch as one array.

options.label: Splunk HEC
options.description: Each event in a HEC envelope with a sourcetype.

options.label: Elastic bulk
options.description: A create action before each event, for a data stream's _bulk endpoint.

options.label: Datadog logs
options.description: Each event as a Datadog log, with a message, source and date.

fields.label: Auth header
fields.help: The header the token is sent in.

fields.label: Auth scheme
fields.help: The word before the token in the header.

options.label: None
options.description: The token is the whole header value.

fields.label: CA certificate
fields.help: PEM certificates to trust for a destination on a private certificate authority. Empty trusts the system's.

fields.label: Extra headers
fields.help: Headers to add, one per line as Name: value. Not encrypted, so not for anything secret.

fields.label: Splunk sourcetype
fields.help: The sourcetype each HEC envelope names.

fields.label: Allow http
fields.help: Post over plain http, unencrypted. Only for a destination on a trusted network.

fields.label: Max body size
fields.help: The most bytes one POST carries; a larger batch goes as several. 0 is no limit, or 5000000 for the Datadog body.

fields.label: Timeout
fields.help: Seconds to wait for the destination to answer a batch.

fields.label: Actions
fields.help: Comma-separated action prefixes to send. Empty sends every event.

fields.label: Exclude
fields.help: Comma-separated action prefixes not to send. app.use, a record of each request to an app, is usually most of the volume; exclude it if your SIEM bills by ingest.

fields.label: Event format
fields.help: How each event is encoded.

options.label: Native
options.description: The event as Pando stores it.

options.label: OCSF
options.description: OCSF 1.3.0, for a SIEM that maps it.

fields.label: Batch size
fields.help: The most events sent in one delivery.

fields.label: Start
fields.help: Where a new destination's first delivery begins. Read once, when Pando first sends to it.

options.label: The oldest event in the live log

presets.label: Splunk HTTP Event Collector
presets.help: In Splunk, Settings > Data inputs > HTTP Event Collector: under Global Settings set All Tokens to Enabled, then choose New Token and copy its value. The URL is your Splunk host on the HEC port, usually 8088, ending /services/collector/event. On Splunk Cloud the host is http-inputs-<stack>.splunkcloud.com on port 443.

presets.label: Datadog Logs
presets.help: In Datadog, Organization Settings > API Keys: choose New Key and set the key as the token. The URL is for the US1 site; for another site use its intake host, such as http-intake.logs.datadoghq.eu for EU or http-intake.logs.us5.datadoghq.com for US5.

presets.label: Elastic
presets.help: In Kibana, open API keys and choose Create API key, with create_doc and auto_configure on the data stream, and set its Encoded value as the token. The URL is your Elasticsearch endpoint, then a data stream name such as logs-pando.audit-default, then /_bulk.

presets.label: Sumo Logic HTTP source
presets.help: In Sumo Logic, Data Management > Data Collection > Collection: choose Add Source beside a hosted collector, then HTTP Logs & Metrics, and copy its HTTP Source Address. The URL contains the source's token, so set it as the secret URL credential and leave url and token empty.

presets.label: Microsoft Sentinel (Azure Monitor Logs ingestion)
presets.help: In Azure, create a data collection rule with a stream named Custom-PandoAudit_CL whose columns match the events, and give the app that mints the token the Monitoring Metrics Publisher role on it. Use the rule's logs ingestion endpoint, or a data collection endpoint's, and its immutable ID in the URL. The token is a Microsoft Entra ID access token for the https://monitor.azure.com scope. This adapter sends a static token and does not mint or refresh one, so a token that expires stops delivery until it is replaced.

do.text: In Splunk, open **Settings** → **Data inputs** → **HTTP Event Collector**.
Under **Global Settings**, set **All Tokens** to **Enabled**.
Choose **New Token**, finish it, and copy its value.
Use your Splunk host on the HEC port, usually `8088`, ending `/services/collector/event`.
On Splunk Cloud, use `https://http-inputs-<stack>.splunkcloud.com/services/collector/event`.
In Datadog, open **Organization Settings** → **API Keys** and choose **New Key**.
Outside US1, change the host to your site's intake host, such as `http-intake.logs.datadoghq.eu`.
In Kibana, open **API keys** and choose **Create API key**.
Grant `create_doc` and `auto_configure` on the data stream.
Copy the **Encoded** value.
Use your Elasticsearch endpoint, then a data stream such as `logs-pando.audit-default`, then `/_bulk`.
In Sumo Logic, open **Data Management** → **Data Collection** → **Collection**.
Choose **Add Source** beside a hosted collector, then **HTTP Logs & Metrics**.
Copy its **HTTP Source Address**.
In Azure, create a data collection rule with a stream named `Custom-PandoAudit_CL`.
Give the app that mints the token the **Monitoring Metrics Publisher** role on it.
Use the rule's logs ingestion endpoint and immutable ID in the URL.
Get a Microsoft Entra ID access token for `https://monitor.azure.com`.
Replace it before it expires: Pando does not refresh it.

kinds.name: Syslog

fields.label: TLS

options.label: On

options.label: Off

fields.label: CA certificate

fields.label: Client key

fields.label: Server name

fields.label: App name

fields.label: Facility

fields.label: Hostname

fields.label: Timeout

fields.label: Actions

fields.label: Exclude
fields.help: Comma-separated action prefixes not to send. app.use, a record of each request to an app, is usually most of the volume; exclude it if your SIEM bills by ingest.

fields.label: Event format

options.description: The event as Pando stores it.

options.label: OCSF
